Head_and_Face: Red eyebrow combs (caruncles) are prominent above the eyes in males.
Beak is short, curved, and dark.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and stocky.
Male (blackcock) exhibits striking bluish-black plumage with iridescent green and purple sheen on the neck and breast.
Most distinctive feature is the white undertail coverts forming a bright white patch visible in flight and during display.
Female (greyhen) is mottled brown and buff with cryptic camouflage patterning.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs and feet are feathered (adaptation for cold climates).
Tail is short and rounded; male tail feathers curve outward in a lyre shape during display.
Wings are broad and rounded for short, explosive flights.

Head_and_Face: Beak is short, curved, and dark.
Eyes are dark with a red eyebrow comb in males.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact and stocky with a short neck and small head.
Most distinctive feature is seasonal plumage change: winter plumage is entirely pure white (except for black tail feathers); summer plumage is mottled brown, grey, and black.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Heavily feathered legs and feet (snowshoe-like adaptation) with dense feathering extending to the toes.
Tail is short and rounded.
Wings are broad and rounded.

Head_and_Face: Beak is short, curved, and dark.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and stocky.
Plumage is mottled brown, grey, and buff with cryptic camouflage patterning.
Two color morphs exist: grey morph (grey-brown with fine vermiculation) and red morph (reddish-brown with darker barring).
Most distinctive feature is the ruff of black feathers on each side of the neck (more prominent in males).
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail is long and broad with a dark subterminal band; tail is fanned during display.
Legs are feathered in winter, bare in summer.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are dark with orange eyebrow combs in males.
Beak is short, curved, and dark.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is stocky and compact.
Plumage is brown mottled with fine barring and vermiculation providing cryptic camouflage.
Males have dark brown body plumage with a banded tail; females are lighter brown with more distinct barring.
Most distinctive features are the orange air sacs on the neck (males only) and the erect pinnae (ear-like feather tufts) on the head.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail is short and rounded.
Legs are feathered to the toes.

Head_and_Face: Fan-like crest of feathers on the head.
Beak is stout and curved.
Body_and_Plumage: Male (peacock) exhibits iridescent blue-green neck and breast plumage.
Most distinctive feature is the enormous elongated upper tail coverts forming the ornamental train (150-200 elongated feathers).
Each train feather is tipped with an iridescent eyespot (ocellus) consisting of concentric rings of blue, gold, and green.
Train measures 120-150 cm in length and is erected and fanned during courtship display.
Female (peahen) is dull brown and grey with cryptic patterning and no train.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are grey with a spur on males.
Body plumage is green and bronze with barred flanks.

Head_and_Face: Beak is short, stout, and curved.
Males often have distinctive facial markings (black throat, white eyebrow stripe, or chestnut face patch depending on species).
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact and rotund.
Plumage is mottled brown, buff, and black with cryptic camouflage patterning.
Most distinctive feature is the short, plump body shape with a small, rounded head and very short tail.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are short and adapted for scratching and running rather than perching.
Wings are short and rounded, adapted for short, explosive flights.
Tail is very short.

Head_and_Face: Beak is short, stout, and curved.
Males often have distinctive facial markings (black throat patch, chestnut face, or white eyebrow stripe depending on species).
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact and stocky.
Plumage is grey-brown with fine barring and vermiculation providing cryptic camouflage.
Most distinctive features include the grey breast (grey partridge) or reddish-brown flanks (red-legged partridge).
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are red or yellow and adapted for scratching and running.
Wings are short and rounded, adapted for short, explosive flights.
Tail is short and rounded.

Head_and_Face: Face is white and bare of feathers around the eyes, creating a distinctive white facial patch.
Beak is large, curved, and black with a prominent cere.
Eyes are dark yellow to amber.
Body_and_Plumage: Body plumage is uniform medium grey with fine scalloping (lighter feather edges) creating a subtle scaled pattern on the breast and belly.
Most distinctive feature is the bright scarlet red tail feathers, contrasting sharply with the grey body.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are grey with zygodactyl feet (two toes forward, two backward) adapted for climbing and manipulating objects.
Wings are broad and rounded.

Head_and_Face: Face is bare of feathers with distinctive skin patch patterns (white with black feather lines or all white) unique to each species.
Beak is massive, strongly curved, and black with a prominent cere.
Eyes are pale yellow to white with a dark pupil.
Body_and_Plumage: Body plumage varies by species but typically includes vivid combinations of red, blue, green, and yellow.
Most common pattern is red body with blue and yellow wing feathers.
Most distinctive feature is the extremely long, graduated tail.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are grey with zygodactyl feet (two toes forward, two backward) adapted for climbing.
Wings are long and pointed.
Tail extends well below the perch.

Head_and_Face: Face is bare of feathers with white skin.
Beak is large, curved, and black with a prominent cere.
Eyes are dark brown with a white eye-ring.
Body_and_Plumage: Body plumage is pure white with a pale yellow wash on the underwing and tail feathers.
Most distinctive feature is the bright sulphur-yellow erectile crest composed of elongated yellow feathers that can be erected into a prominent fan-shaped display.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are grey with zygodactyl feet (two toes forward, two backward) adapted for climbing.
Wings are broad and rounded.
Tail is moderately long and rounded.
